parameters.content:
## Before you run: change these 5 things

1. **Webhook** → Path: pick your own name.
2. **Check Verify Token** → replace `CHANGE_ME_VERIFY_TOKEN` with your own secret, and put the SAME value in Meta → Webhooks.
3. **Mark as Read** → Credential: Header Auth (`Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>`).
4. **Log Incoming Message** + **Update WhatsApp Status** → Credential: your Postgres. Run the table SQL first.
5. **Config** → `supabase_url` and `system_prompt`.

**Then:** Publish → test GET with curl → register the webhook in Meta (fields: messages) → send a message.

Warning: the pinData on Webhook is FAKE sample data for teaching. Unpin it before production.
Never put a token / App Secret / PIN inside any node.

## How this workflow works

**GET** (once): Meta sends verify_token + challenge → if the token matches we echo the challenge back.

**POST** (every event): respond 200 immediately → Config → Event Type:
- **messages** → Parse → Log to DB → if new → Mark as Read → Message Type → (your replies)
- **statuses** → Parse → Update status of an outgoing message

Note: messages YOU send never arrive on the webhook. Log them yourself after every send (direction = outgoing, wa_message_id from the API response).

### 1) Webhook
**Change the Path** to your own name.
The URL you give to Meta:
`https://<n8n-domain>/webhook/<Path>`
GET + POST must both be enabled.

### 2) Verify Token
Replace `CHANGE_ME_VERIFY_TOKEN` with your own secret.
Put **exactly the same value** in:
Meta App → WhatsApp → Configuration → Verify token

### 3) Config
Change `supabase_url` and `system_prompt`.
Leave `phone_number_id`: it is read from the webhook automatically.
Keep one `graph_version` across the whole workflow.

### 4) Postgres Credential
Select your database credential.
Run `supabase_whatsapp_messages_table.sql` in Supabase SQL Editor **before** the first message.

### 5) WhatsApp Credential
Header Auth:
- Name: `Authorization`
- Value: `Bearer <TOKEN>`
The token lives in the credential only. **Never in the node.**

### 6) Postgres Credential
Same credential as #4.
Updates the status of **outgoing** messages only (the ones you logged after sending).

### 7) Your replies go here
Every branch (Text / Media / Location / Button / Unsupported) is empty on purpose.
After each one add: HTTP Request node (send) + Postgres node (log the outgoing message, direction = outgoing).

nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes:
GET = Meta verification (once, when you register the webhook). POST = every message and status.
Change the Path to your own name. Webhook URL: https://<n8n-domain>/webhook/<Path>

nodes.name: Check Verify Token
nodes.notes: Replace CHANGE_ME_VERIFY_TOKEN with your own secret. The exact same value goes in Meta → App → WhatsApp → Configuration → Verify token.

nodes.name: Return Challenge
nodes.notes: Echoes hub.challenge as plain text with HTTP 200. Returning JSON here makes Meta reject the webhook.

nodes.name: Reject
nodes.notes: Wrong verify token → 403 with no body.

nodes.name: Ack Message
nodes.notes: Always respond 200 immediately, before any processing. If we are slow, Meta re-sends the same event (up to 36 hours).

nodes.name: Parse Message
nodes.notes:
Turns the webhook into one item per message: phone / user_id (BSUID) / reply_to / type / content / button_reply / media_id / location...
Always reply to reply_to (phone ?? user_id) to support users with hidden numbers.

nodes.name: Event Type
nodes.notes: messages = a message from a user. statuses = delivery update for a message WE sent.

nodes.name: Parse Status
nodes.notes: One item per status: wamid + sent/delivered/read/failed + timestamp + failure reason if any.

parameters.query:
update public.whatsapp_messages
set status    = $2::text,
    status_at = to_timestamp($4::bigint),
    error     = case when $2::text = 'failed' then nullif($3, '') else error end,
    user_id   = coalesce(user_id, nullif($5, ''))
where wa_message_id = $1
  and direction = 'outgoing'
  and (
    $2::text = 'failed'
    or coalesce(array_position(array['sent','delivered','read'], status), 0)
     < array_position(array['sent','delivered','read'], $2::text)
  )
returning id, wa_message_id, status;

nodes.name: Update WhatsApp Status
nodes.notes:
Updates outgoing messages (the ones you logged after sending). sent → delivered → read never goes backwards; failed overrides any status.
Credential: your Postgres.

parameters.query:
insert into public.whatsapp_messages
  (wa_message_id, phone, user_id, direction, message_type, content,
   button_reply, button_title, raw)
values (
  $1, nullif($2, ''), nullif($3, ''), 'incoming', $4, nullif($5, ''),
  nullif($6, ''), nullif($7, ''), $8::jsonb
)
on conflict (wa_message_id) do nothing
returning id;

nodes.name: Log Incoming Message
nodes.notes:
Inserts every incoming message into whatsapp_messages. on conflict do nothing = if Meta sends the same message twice, it is stored once. $1,$2.. come from queryReplacement (never concatenate values into SQL).
Credential: your Postgres. The table must exist first (SQL file shipped with this workflow).

assignments.name: system_prompt
assignments.value: You are the WhatsApp assistant for [Company Name]. Reply in Egyptian Arabic, friendly and short (1-4 lines). If you do not know something, say so honestly and never invent information.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes:
All settings in one place. phone_number_id is read from the webhook itself (not hardcoded), so this works for any number under the same App.
Change supabase_url and system_prompt. Keep graph_version identical in every node (v26.0).

nodes.name: Is New Message?
nodes.notes: If Meta re-sent the same message, on conflict returns no id → stop here so we never reply twice.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ messaging_product: 'whatsapp', status: 'read', message_id: $('Parse Message').item.json.message_id, typing_indicator: { type: 'text' } }) }}

nodes.name: Mark as Read
nodes.notes:
Credential: Header Auth → Name: Authorization / Value: Bearer <TOKEN>. Token lives in the credential only, never in the node.
Sends blue double ticks + typing indicator. onError = continue so a failure here never blocks the reply.

nodes.name: Message Type
nodes.notes: Build your replies from here: Text / Media / Location / Button / Silent / Unsupported. Every branch is intentionally empty.
